messages:
Sara Patel: Heads-up — ran a tiled/interleaved KV layout experiment on flash2 vs paged-fused kernels and hit a weird perf regression on seq_len=1024 workloads. numbers below.
Matt O'Neill: Ugh, regression where exactly? kernel time, memcpy, or cache thrash?
Sara Patel: Kernel time + L2 churn. baseline (flash2 contiguous KV) avg token = 6.8 ms per token. tiled/interleaved KV with 16KB tiles -> 8.3 ms (+22%). observed a ~2x increase in L2 misses.
Jia Chen: Did dtype change? float16 vs bfloat16 can change access patterns due to alignment.
Sara Patel: We tested both. config snippet:
```
kv_layout:
  mode: interleaved-tiles
  tile_bytes: 16384
  align: 256
  dtype: bfloat16
```
Switching to float16 dropped kernel by 0.5 ms but memcpy and uncoalesced loads spiked for some batch shapes.
Eli Rodriguez: Any evidence it's stride/alignment causing uncoalesced loads? page-boundary crossing?
Sara Patel: Yes — captured an nsys heaptrace showing repeated memcpy around tile boundaries. stack shows flash_attn_tiled calling load_kv_tile -> fallback_copy when (addr % 256) != 0.
infra-bot: nsys summary uploaded: https://ci/reports/1722109876/nsys-summary.html :file_folder: 
Matt O'Neill: Can you paste the nvprof excerpt?
Sara Patel: Sure, quick nvprof: 
```
GPU activities:
  GPU memcpy HtoD: 0.31 ms
  GPU kernel: flash_attn_tiled (grid=256x, time=8.27 ms)
  GPU kernel: flash_attn_fused (grid=200x, time=6.72 ms)
Counters:
  L2 read hits: 9.5e8
  L2 read misses: 5.6e6  (tiled) vs 2.7e6 (contig)
  DRAM throughput: 120 GB/s (tiled) vs 88 GB/s (contig)
```
Jia Chen: DRAM throughput up but kernel slower -> likely memory divergence/uncoalesced causing more transactions. also bfloat16 alignment 4 bytes vs 2 bytes for float16 matters with vector loads.
Eli Rodriguez: Did you try changing align to 128 or 64? maybe 256 is too strict causing extra padding and page splits.
Sara Patel: Yup. align=128 improved L2 misses (~+10% vs baseline) and kernel time 7.1 ms, but still worse in some micro-batches. align=64 brought us within noise of baseline for float16, but bfloat16 remained slightly worse.
Matt O'Neill: How about separate KV layout (keys contiguous, values contiguous) vs interleaved tiles? I remember interleaved helped when avg seq_len low, but maybe at 1024 interleaving causes strided accesses.
Sara Patel: Exactly. Separate layout (no interleaving) made access contiguous for our attention window pattern and gave 6.9 ms — basically baseline. But separate layout increases page table entries for small seqs. tradeoffs.
Jia Chen: Any batching heuristics interaction? big dynamic batches could cross tile boundaries and amplify the problem.
Sara Patel: We saw that too. Our default continuous-batching heuristic was grouping requests until either token budget or timeout. when a large request (seq 1024) got batched with many small ones, the tiled loader did extra scatter-gather per request, creating O(N_tiles) overhead.
Eli Rodriguez: Could we add a quick heuristic: if any request seq_len > tile_bytes / dtype_size / heads_threshold then use separate layout or fall back to flash_fused?
Matt O'Neill: I like a policy switch. Also we should expose a runtime flag kv_tile_align and a metric: tile_boundary_cross_count. Alert when > X% of ops hit boundary copies.
Sara Patel: Added that to the profiling run. Here is a flame snippet from nsight showing hot path at load_kv_tile -> memcpy -> flash_attn_tiled.
```
Frame 1: load_kv_tile (30%)
Frame 2: memcpy (12%)
Frame 3: flash_attn_tiled (45%)
```
Jia Chen: Could also try kernel-level prefetching of next tile to hide memcpy, or using unified contiguous staging buffer per batch to aggregate small tile copies into a single D2H/H2D.
Eli Rodriguez: Prefetch sounds promising but increases memory residency; need to check tail latencies.
Matt O'Neill: Quick action items: 1) Add tile_boundary_cross_count metric & kv_tile_align flag (Sara) 2) Canonical benchmark run across seq_lengths [128,512,1024,2048] with bfloat16/float16 and interleaved/separate (Jia) 3) Prototype fallback policy in router: prefer fused-contig for seq>threshold (Eli) 4) Upload nsys + nvprof artifacts to perf bucket (infra-bot)
Sara Patel: I'll push the metric and initial fallback patch today. early PR will expose kv_tile_align in runtime config and a runtime warning logging when we hit >2% boundary copies.
infra-bot: perf artifacts copied to s3://redwood-perf/1722109876/ (nvprof, nsys, heaptrace)
Matt O'Neill: Thanks. If the fallback reduces token p99 or evens out DRAM throughput, we'll add an automated rule in Optimize to recommend layout per workload. :thumbsup:
Sara Patel: Yep — aim to have benchmark matrix results by EOD tomorrow. Will post numbers in this thread.
Jia Chen: Nice investigation. small follow-up: can you capture the raw stride sequences for a couple of culprit batches? that'll help us write a unit test for coalescing.
Sara Patel: On it. attaching a short script to dump strides (will upload next update).
Eli Rodriguez: Good. If we can reproduce with synthetic strides, we can add a microkernel test to CI. low-risk.
Sara Patel: Uploaded stride dumps and perf matrix CSV to the perf bucket. Closing loop when benchmarks finish. :raised_hands:
